summary.oneLiner: HMVL is the Hindi-print (Hindustan masthead) operating arm of HT Media Group with a strong, cash-rich balance sheet (group net cash >INR 1,000 cr). The FY26 story is one of **profitability cleanup**: Print delivered double-digit ad growth driven almost entirely by **yield/pricing** (volumes flat, tracking industry), while the group decisively exited/wound down loss-making lines — OTTplay (Digital) discontinued and six non-viable Radio frequencies surrendered. Margins expanded ~100bps. The two-edged risk: (a) rising newsprint cost amplified by weak rupee, and (b) a large treasury that took mark-to-market hits from record-high bond yields, dragging other income. No capital return signalled — cash earmarked for "businesses of tomorrow" (core print copies + Digital/Digicontent).

scorecard:
**Consolidated GROUP (HT Media) figures unless tagged HMVL:**

| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | FY26 (full year) | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Total revenue (group) | INR 558 cr | −2% | flat | flat | Stable on annual basis |
| EBITDA (group) | INR 131 cr | +5% | INR 298 cr | +8% | Margin +100bps |
| EBITDA margin (group) | 23% | +100bps | — | +100bps | |
| PAT reported (group) | INR 96 cr | — | INR 153 cr | — | FY26 PAT margin 8% |
| Net cash / treasury (group) | — | — | **>INR 1,000 cr** | — | "robust", "patient capital" |
| **Print** op revenue (group) | INR 427 cr | — | INR 1,500 cr | +8% | |
| **Print** ad revenue | INR 313 cr | +10% | INR 1,148 cr | +8% | Yield-led |
| **Print** circulation | INR 51 cr | +4% | ~flat | — | |
| **Print** op EBITDA | INR 97 cr | — | INR 208 cr | — | margin 23% Q / 14% FY |
| Print **HMVL/Hindi** ad | INR 142 cr | +12% | INR 504 cr | +8% | |
| Print **HMVL/Hindi** circ | INR 38 cr | ~flat | INR 155 cr | ~flat | |
| Print **English** ad | INR 172 cr | +9% | INR 644 cr | +8% | |
| Print **English** circ | INR 13 cr | +13% | INR 53 cr | −5% | Q4 uptick on copies |
| Radio (group) op rev | INR 43 cr | decline | INR 140 cr | decline | EBITDA −7cr Q / −22cr FY |
| Digital (group) op rev | INR 39 cr | flat | INR 155 cr | flat | EBITDA −2cr Q / −8cr FY; restated for continuing ops |

**One-offs / non-recurring (CRITICAL):**
- **HMVL other operating income ~INR 32 cr in Q4** (≈2x prior-year ~INR 16 cr) — driven by **AFE contract forfeitures** (contractual ad-space revenue forfeited when counterparty fails to use it in the specified window). Non-cash AFE, lumpy/non-recurring.
- **Other income (interest) down ~INR 50 cr** FY26 (INR 168 cr vs INR 218 cr FY25) — caused by **mark-to-market losses on the treasury book** as bond yields hit record highs (10Y ~7%). Mgmt expects reversal as curve stabilises ("patient capital").
- **Exceptional / discontinued-ops losses (group, FY26):** ~INR 114 cr exceptional loss from continuing ops + ~INR 101 cr loss from discontinued ops = **~INR 215 cr** total (per analyst, mgmt acknowledged). Includes a large item tied to new **Government labour codes**.
- **HMVL segment-revenue restated** ~INR 6 cr lower (Print ~INR 667.23 cr vs ~INR 673 cr reported earlier) — removal of OTTplay intersegment ad revenue, now in discontinued ops; PBIT down equally.
guidance (critical):
- **No formal revenue/earnings guidance** given (standard policy).
- **No further closure/exceptional losses from business side** — portfolio "cleaned up as much as possible." Caveat: statutory items (labour codes) could still hit if anything further crystallises.
- **OTTplay:** only "very small / rounding-off" residual P&L impact in FY27 from servicing pre-31-Mar subscriptions (1–6 month life, up to ~Sep). Some **cash outflow** to exit content/ISP/channel-partner contracts. No residual sale value (capital-light biz; no buyer found).
- **Ad yields:** management hopes/plans to hold deals "at a certain level and above, not below" for FY27 — but flagged competitive reaction risk; explicitly declined a "carte blanche" on sustainability.
pipeline / order book: - No traditional order pipeline (media). **AFE portfolio** (ads-for-equity assets) is the closest analogue: mix of fully matured, semi-matured and "under-baked" assets; managed as a portfolio to maximise cash. Active (not desperate) sellers; ~4–5 yr track record of monetisation. AFE acquisitions are always **non-cash** (paid in ad space).
segment detail (print / digital / treasu:
- **Print (core, HMVL=Hindi):** strongest leg; ad +10% group / +12% HMVL-Hindi, yield-led. Circulation +4% group on copies (English +13% Q on copies); company deliberately buying **copy share** market-by-market (short-term trade-off for long-term gain), financed by yield gains. Realisation per copy up only marginally (competition cap).
- **Radio (group, not in HMVL):** under pressure; high prior-year event base. **Six loss-making frequencies surrendered** to GoI; remaining stations all profitable. Will keep reviewing.
- **Digital (group, not in HMVL):** Shine + Mosaic core; **OTTplay discontinued** (telco competition, unit economics never worked even in Tier 2/3 strategy). Digital flagged as future priority — but core print remains the near-term engine.
- **Treasury:** >INR 1,000 cr net cash; "patient capital"; took MTM hits in FY26.
growth / optionality:
- Ad **pricing/yield** is the primary lever (volumes flat) — re-rating optionality if structural.
- **Copy-share gains** in key markets = future ad-base optionality.
- **Treasury reversal** optionality: ~INR 50 cr other-income drag could reverse if yields normalise.
- **Digital/Digicontent** investments positioned as long-term optionality funded by cash pile.
- **AFE monetisation** as recurring lumpy cash/value-unlock.
margins & cost (newsprint):
- Group EBITDA margin 23% Q4 (+100bps); Print margin 23% Q / 14% FY.
- **Key cost risk: rising newsprint cost**, amplified by **weakening rupee** + global supply-chain / trade-policy / geopolitical disruption. Chairperson flagged as the near-term concern; managed via "cost discipline."
capex: - No formal capex guidance. Investment is being directed into **circulation/copies** (working-capital-like, core print) and into **Digital/Digicontent**, rather than heavy fixed capex. OTTplay described as "not capital-heavy."
capital allocation (cash / buyback):
- Group net cash **>INR 1,000 cr**. Board "always discusses the cash pile."
- Stated priority: **invest in "businesses of tomorrow"** (core print copies + Digital/Digicontent).
- **No buyback / no dividend / no capital return** signalled — explicitly "there is none so far" when asked about returning cash to shareholders.
risks (print decline & others):
- **Newsprint cost inflation + INR depreciation** — primary near-term margin risk.
- **Treasury MTM** sensitivity to bond yields (record-high 10Y ~7%).
- **Ad-yield sustainability** — competitive reaction could erode pricing gains; volumes flat.
- **Radio** structurally under pressure (industry-wide).
- **Statutory / labour-code** liabilities could trigger further exceptionals.
- Secular **print decline** / digital migration — long-term structural overhang.
management tone: Confident and candid. CFO welcomed analyst praise for the loss-making cleanup ("better late than never" sentiment echoed approvingly). Transparent on one-offs (forfeitures, MTM, exceptionals) and willing to say "no" on guidance/competitive data. Framing: profitability discipline now, growth optionality later. Positive but measured on ad-yield durability.
non-obvious takeaways:
- **HMVL's ~INR 32 cr "other operating income" is largely AFE forfeiture income** — a non-cash, lumpy item that flatters the standalone P&L; investors should normalise it out.
- **Assetvault (AasaanWill)** — INR 22 cr "investment" is an **AFE (non-cash ad-space) deal**, not a cash outlay, into an unrelated will-services business with ~nil revenue after 8 years; framed as marketing-partnership optionality.
- The **~INR 50 cr other-income drop is MTM, not operational** — likely reverses, so reported PAT understates underlying treasury earning power.
- Net cash >INR 1,000 cr is **large relative to a print-media micro/small-cap** — significant balance-sheet cushion, but management explicitly will NOT return it; deployment into "businesses of tomorrow" carries capital-allocation/value-destruction risk (cf. OTTplay).
- AFE assets are always acquired non-cash (ad inventory) → low downside, real upside on monetisation.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ Beneficiaries: (none cleanly identifiable from this call)
- ⭐ Watch: companies/platforms gaining from print's structural ad-yield resilience in Hindi/Tier-2/3 markets; potential AFE-asset counterparties.

OTTplay discontinued; 6 Radio frequencies surrendered; FY26 exceptional+discontinued losses ~INR 215 cr (incl. labour-code item). HMVL other op income ~INR 32 cr (AFE forfeiture). Other income −INR 50 cr YoY on treasury MTM. No capital return. No further closure losses guided (statutory caveat).

themes.title: Media, entertainment & out-of-home advertising
themes.need: Digital-content, music-IP licensing and an advertising-recovery cycle underpin media - TIPSMUSIC on music IP; ZEEL/ENIL/RADIOCITY/BTML on broadcast/content; HTMEDIA/DBCORP/HMVL on print + digital; SIGNPOST/BRIGHT-tier and UFO on OOH/cinema. Ad-spend revival is the near-term swing factor.
themes.driver: Festive ad-spend recovery; music-licensing/streaming monetization; OOH inventory uptake.
